verdicts.strongest_argument: I agree with the finding's premise and that is exactly why it scores near the top of the scale: there was no distinct earnings event on 2026-09-03 for this name. Two 6-Ks reporting the quarter ended 30 June 2026 were filed on 2026-09-02 (filings.json), the baseline's event_plausibility is 'unknown' with cadence_implausible and last_print 2026-09-02 one day earlier, and the reaction is already in the bars the baseline seals - the history records the 09-02 event at -4.83%, and run_up_5d is -8.96% with run_up_20d -18.20% into a 09-03 close of 3.92. Once the release is out and the market has traded two sessions on it, the results are the price by definition; a claim whose own headline is 'the results are already out' cannot also be an unpriced fact. What the finding actually asserts is drift - that an illiquid nano-cap takes several days to re-rate a strategy reversal - and that is a momentum hypothesis, not information, with no dated source and no size. There is also a methodological problem with its evidence that I have to flag, because it follows from the finding's own dating: if the release was made on 09-02, then snapshots/20260903T150908Z.json is post-release material and the quote it leans on ('very disappointing... today after 1 year, ended up in confused out of focus...') is post-print reaction commentary, not pre-print evidence. The hunter labels that snapshot admissible on the basis of the tagged after-the-close 09-03 session while simultaneously arguing the release preceded it; those two positions cannot both hold. Finally, the closing argument - 'if it were priced the stock would not have needed a 1-for-8 reverse split three weeks ago' - is a non sequitur: the split was a listing mechanic completed on 08-19 and says nothing about whether the September results are in the price.

The two sessions spanning the release are down and the stock is within 4.5% of its 52-week low - the reset is in the price, not ahead of it. event_plausibility is cadence_implausible with a 2-day inferred cadence, confirming the 09-03 row is stale.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: Evidence of a separate, additional disclosure on 2026-09-03 - a distinct 6-K, a conference call transcript, a partnership announcement - rather than the 09-02 filings the finding itself identifies.

verdicts.strongest_argument: This is the better of the two and I put it in the middle rather than the refuted band, but two things hold it there. First, it is half published already: the at-the-market selling the finding treats as its discovery is being narrated in the captured stream by retail participants on 2026-08-24 ('looks like they ATM'ing', 'I was thinking that the CEO was using Galmed as an ATM', docs/8c2c7f33148bf6712100e164894cff256da07b40.txt), and the 424B3 prospectuses of 06-08 and 06-22 plus the POS EX are all in filings.json, so the supply mechanism is both reachable and being discussed. The POS AM of 09-02 is a housekeeping amendment that I agree no aggregator surfaces - that part is genuinely quiet, which is why this is not lower. Second, and against it: a live shelf and continuous ATM issuance at a clinical-stage nano-cap with a $4.3m market cap that has just reverse-split to hold its listing is the definition of structural and known. Every holder of a company in this condition prices dilution as the base case, and the 20-day chart shows exactly that - -18.2% into the print with the stock 4.5% off its 52-week low. The finding also has no size: no POS AM body is stored, so there is no registered amount, no remaining capacity and no daily-volume cap to weigh against the 35,620-share average. Dilution is the dominant force in this name, but it was the dominant force last month too.

A stock grinding to its 52-week low on tiny volume through a live shelf is a tape already absorbing continuous supply; the marginal news content of one more post-effective amendment against that is small.
